processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots of nominal Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %) in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated 17Al sample aged at 550 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching (defines this sample / process proc_aging-550c-3h).

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase α (Body-centered cubic, BCC) structure in the solution-treated state (before aging); the 17Al IPF map shows coarse grains.

Partially transformed α + β-Mn structure; after aging the 17Al alloy at 550 °C for 3 h the matrix shows faint grain-boundary contrast and only partial α → β-Mn transformation (complete transformation of 17Al at 550 °C required 6 h).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s, average of 5 measurements

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, value = average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 550 °C for 3 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 3 h shows 669.2 ± 24.9 HV

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging; 50 µm scale bar on main fields (2 or 10 µm insets)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 8 panel 550 °C - 3 h (17Al): partially transformed matrix with faint grain-boundary contrast

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine constituent phases and their evolution during aging of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); α progressively transforms to β-Mn with aging, with new BCC and FCC phases appearing inside β-Mn at higher temperatures

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: Both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks together with α/D0₃ were found, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and HRTEM
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: foils mechanically ground to ~90 μm, punched to 3 mm diameter, ion thinned
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the microstructures of the ultra-high-hardness alloys (β-Mn, FCC Cu-rich phase, FCC twins)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins distributed at β-Mn interfaces in the hardest samples

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced ≥ 5 μm apart; samples mechanically polished
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine intrinsic hardness of β-Mn and micro-hardness of the ultra-hard samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardest 17Al sample average nanoindentation hardness 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa; intrinsic β-Mn hardness 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM (ZEISS Sigma 300) EDS; TEM (FEI Talos F200X) EDS detector
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure alloy chemical composition and determine the composition of β-Mn and the FCC Cu-rich phase
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al alloy composition Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%); Cu-rich FCC precipitates depleted in Fe and Mn

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, the α → β-Mn transformation at 550 °C was completed only after 6 h of aging, so the 550 °C/3 h condition of this sample corresponds to an incompletely (partially) transformed α + β-Mn microstructure (b0065, b0053).
The 17Al alloy (Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu) chemical composition measured by EDS: Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%) [Table 1, b0013]; measured density by Archimedes method = 6.76 g·cm⁻³ [b0017].
The peak hardness of the 17Al alloy (924.9 HV) was achieved by aging at 575 °C for 6 h — a different aging condition from this sample (b0037, b0038, Table 3).
Along the alloy series, increasing Al content slows the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn: at 550 °C the α → β-Mn transformation of 17Al became essentially complete after 6 h (b0053, b0065).
